> **Conclusion.** We ran {{rows}} published uses on a world model that cost ${{cost_w1}} to train. We find that the encoder can tell a success from a failure after the fact, and that the predictor does not add to that; training on up to {{sc5_eps}} episodes did not change this. For ranking chunks, the commanded actions, which need no model, were better than the predictor. Our results suggest that before a learned predictor is built into a pipeline on a rig of this kind, its contribution should be measured against the encoder alone and against the commanded actions on the same rows.

> **Conclusion.** We launched {{rows}} tests on a latent world model that took ${{cost_w1}} to train. We found out that the encoder can detect a successful run from a failure after the task is done, without the predictor playing a significant role. Training on {{sc5_eps}} episodes did not improve this. To rank chunks, the commanded actions, which did not need any model, were better than the predictor. This means that before adding a learned predictor to a pipeline, even on a rig such as ours, its contribution needs to be measured against the encoder by itself and the commanded actions.
